mainLabels.label: Enemy Image
mainLabels.description: Enemy Image describes how language can portray an outgroup as an enemy. The group appears dangerous, immoral, or fundamentally different. This can make violence against them seem more acceptable, reduce moral hesitation, and mobilize the ingroup.

subLabels.label: Homogenization
subLabels.description: Homogenization describes statements in which an outgroup is presented as one uniform mass and individual differences disappear.

subLabels.label: Immutability
subLabels.description: Immutability describes statements in which a group is presented as unchangeable, permanently hostile, or unable to reform.

subLabels.label: Essentialization
subLabels.description: Essentialization means that an outgroup is presented as having a negative nature. It is not only about individual actions, but about how the whole group is described. The group is linked to certain traits, behaviors, or values. This makes it appear fundamentally different from the ingroup. Essentialization can also be indirect. For example, cruel or abusive treatment of children can create a very negative image of the whole group, because children stand for innocence and vulnerability. Such portrayals can make violence against the outgroup seem more acceptable or necessary.

subLabels.label: Dehumanization
subLabels.description: Dehumanization describes statements in which people are linguistically removed from the sphere of human dignity and protection.

subLabels.label: Threat Depiction
subLabels.description: Threat depiction describes statements that mark a group, person, or situation as an acute threat.

mainLabels.label: Just Cause
mainLabels.description: Presents coercive, violent, or restrictive action as justified by security, self-defence, counterterrorism, or retaliation.

subLabels.label: Security rationale
subLabels.description: Security rationale describes statements that legitimize measures through security, protection, or risk prevention.

subLabels.label: Self-defence / counterterrorism
subLabels.description: Self-defence / counterterrorism describes statements that frame actions as self-defence or counterterrorism.

subLabels.label: Retaliation
subLabels.description: Retaliation describes statements in which violence or coercion is justified as an answer, reprisal, or necessary response.

mainLabels.label: Individual Needs
mainLabels.description: Links support for action to psychological needs such as meaning, status, belonging, confidence, or the promise of victory.

subLabels.label: Meaning
subLabels.description: Meaning describes statements that charge actions with purpose, mission, or historical significance.

subLabels.label: Status
subLabels.description: Status describes statements that emphasize strength, rank, recognition, or national self-assertion.

subLabels.label: Hope for victory
subLabels.description: Hope for victory describes statements that mobilize support through the prospect of victory, strength, or successful enforcement.

mainLabels.label: Rhetorical Foreclosure
mainLabels.description: Closes down alternatives by portraying restraint, compromise, humanitarian concern, or external criticism as weakness, betrayal, or impossibility.

subLabels.label: No alternative framing
subLabels.description: No alternative framing describes statements in which alternatives are excluded or presented as impossible.

subLabels.label: Humanity as weakness
subLabels.description: Humanity as weakness describes statements in which humanitarian restraint is framed as weakness or danger.

subLabels.label: External criticism rejection
subLabels.description: External criticism rejection describes statements that reject external criticism as illegitimate, hostile, or fundamentally irrelevant.
